title: Hybrid Inference Sell-through Kit: Technical Positioning, Pricing Scenarios, and Security FAQ
author: Eleanor Park
content:
Summary:

This document is a compact sell-through kit designed for field sellers and SEs engaging mid-market and enterprise buyers who are evaluating hybrid inference architectures (hosted API + private/Dedicated deployments). It bundles concise positioning, a competitive brief, two short case studies, recommended slide flow for a 20-minute technical pitch, sample pricing scenarios, and a prospect-facing security FAQ. Use this as the canonical one-pager to tailor follow-ups and create customer-facing slide decks.

Audience:
- Technical buyer (ML/Platform/Infra)
- Product/Feature owner evaluating cost, latency, and compliance tradeoffs
- Procurement/security reviewers who will sign off on deployment model

1) One-line value props (quick soundbites)
- For engineers: "Ship consistent, low-latency LLM inference across cloud and on-prem with the same API and rollout controls."
- For infra/platform: "Predictable throughput with reserved Dedicated pools and autoscaling policies reduces tail latency and operational toil."
- For security/compliance: "Private deployments with customer-managed VPC and KMS integrations meet common regulatory controls without re-architecting your stack."

2) Core differentiation pillars (3 bullets with backing statements)
- Unified runtime & API: Single SDK and model catalog across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private reduces work required for multi-environment deployments and simplifies testing (same model versioning and rollout semantics).
- Cost-aware serving controls: Batching/caching suggestions, quantization profiles, and routing policies let customers reduce per-token cost by 20–60% in practice depending on workload shape. We ship telemetry that maps these levers to expected $/1M tokens.
- Reliability and automatic graceful degradation: Smart routing + model fallbacks keep customer apps online when capacity or regions are constrained. Built-in canaries and line-item observability reduce regression risk.

3) Competitive brief (executive table you can read out in 2 minutes)
| Dimension | Redwood Inference | Major cloud LLM APIs | Self-hosted OSS runtimes | Inference-specialized vendors |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Deployment models | Hosted / Dedicated / Private (VPC & on-prem) | Hosted ± partner integrations | On-prem only | Hosted or on-prem but limited ecosystem |
| Unified API across modes | Yes | No (hosted only) | Varies | Varies |
| Pricing control (batching/quantization) | Built-in recommendations + telemetry | Minimal | Manual | Partial |
| SLOs & enterprise SLAs | SLA for Dedicated + observability | SLA varies by provider | Customer-managed | Vendor-dependent |
| Security integrations | KMS/HSM, VPC, audit logs | Cloud-native tooling only | Depends | Select integrations |
| Typical buyer wins | Platform teams, regulated enterprises | Rapid prototypes | RL/infra-first teams | Cost-conscious deployments |

Callout: When the conversation is purely cost-centric with engineering bandwidth to self-host, OSS is competitive. For regulated customers needing a low-ops private plane or predictable burst capacity for production, Redwood’s Dedicated + Private options accelerate time-to-production and reduce long-term total cost of ownership.

4) Two short customer vignettes (1–2 paragraphs each)
- FinOps SaaS (Mid-market) — "SmartInvoice": needed sub-300ms latency for the summarization microservice and data residency for EU customers. Implemented Redwood Dedicated pools (1x p4d-equivalent reserved + burst), configured prefix caching for standard invoice templates, and applied int8 quantization profile recommended by Redwood Optimize. Result: 45% reduction in per-request cost, median p50 latency 220ms, and compliance review completed in 6 weeks.

- Regulated Healthcare Enterprise — "Horizon Health": required on-prem inference for PHI plus centralized observability for product owners. Deployed Redwood Private (air-gapped bundle) with KMS integration and automated rollout policy that mirrors hosted behavior. Eng team reused the same API tests and eval prompts from hosted staging environment, reducing validation time by 60%.

5) Recommended 20-minute field pitch flow (slide-by-slide + talking points)
- Slide 1 (2 min): Problem & Impact — show customer-specific cost/latency regressions and compliance constraints.
- Slide 2 (3 min): Redwood value props — unified API, reserved capacity, private plane. Use the one-liners above.
- Slide 3 (4 min): Architecture options — quick diagrams for Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private with switching/fallback behavior.
- Slide 4 (3 min): Risk & mitigation — model quality regressions, capacity limits, data egress. Explain canaries and automatic fallbacks.
- Slide 5 (4 min): Pricing scenarios — show sample math for 3 workload archetypes (below).
- Slide 6 (2 min): Security & compliance summary — answer common checklist items.
- Slide 7 (2 min): Next steps & pilot proposal — propose scope, success metrics, timeline (pilot = 6 weeks).

6) Pricing guidance & sample scenarios (high-level; use for commercial discussions, not a binding quote)
Assumptions (example): p1) 5M tokens/day; 2) mix 70% generation, 30% embeddings; 3) commit to Dedicated baseline of 2 GPUs; 4) predicted batching and caching yield 30% token reduction.
- Quick-tier math (hosted): baseline hosted list-rate = $0.0008 per generation token (example). Estimated monthly spend: 5M tokens/day x 30 days x $0.0008 = $120,000/month. After batching/caching guidance (30% reduction): $84,000/month.
- Dedicated scenario: Reserved capacity (2 x rtx-a6000-equivalent) = $40k/month committed + usage overage at $0.00045 per token. With caching reductions, total estimated = $40k + (5M*30*0.00045*0.7) ≈ $43k/month.
- Private (on-prem): Platform license + deployment and ops retainer. Typical structure: one-time packaging + integration fee (~$120k) + annual platform license (~$200k) + optional support. TCO advantage appears for sustained > ~100M tokens/month and strict compliance needs.

Pricing callouts for negotiation:
- Emphasize predictability of Dedicated commitments vs variable hosted spend.
- Offer a measured pilot: 6-week committed Dedicated at ~50% of expected steady-state to validate latency and unit economics.
- For strategic accounts, we can layer a 3–6 month ramp with graduated commit discounts.

7) Objections & short rebuttals
- "We can just self-host and save money." — If your team has >1 FTE dedicated to infra and SRE, OSS can work. For product teams needing fast iteration, Redwood removes operational burden and provides observability and SLAs that accelerate product launches.
- "We can’t send data to hosted services." — Private deployments with VPC and on-prem packaging address most regulated needs; discuss the specific control (KMS/HSM, audit logs, network isolation) the customer requires.
- "We need peak throughput that varies monthly." — Recommend Dedicated + burst policies and smart routing; autoscaling policies and regional fallbacks mitigate spikes without overcommitting.

8) Prospect-facing Security FAQ (copyable into an RFP response)
Q: What deployment options support PHI and regulated data?
A: Redwood supports Private (on-prem and VPC) and Dedicated with customer-controlled networking. Private deployments can be delivered as an air-gapped package; Dedicated can be configured with private peering and strict egress controls.

Q: How is encryption handled at rest and in transit?
A: TLS 1.2+ for in-transit. At-rest encryption via customer-managed KMS keys (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or HSM-backed keys on request). Audit logs include key rotation events and access records.

Q: Do you support Bring Your Own Key (BYOK)?
A: Yes — BYOK via standard KMS integrations is supported for both Dedicated and Private deployments.

Q: How do you provide auditability for model inference?
A: Request-level logging with metadata (model version, route, request id, latency, token counts) stored in customer-controlled retention buckets. Full audit trails are available in Private deployments; Hosted retains logs per tenant with configurable retention windows.

Q: What certifications / compliance evidence do you provide?
A: We publish SOC 2 Type II reports for the hosted control plane and provide architecture diagrams, data flow docs, and assessor-friendly evidence packages to support customer audits for Dedicated and Private engagements.

Q: How are vulnerabilities in models handled?
A: We provide model vetting guidance and can operate a controlled model onboarding workflow: static checks, test prompt-sets, and staged rollout with canaries. For Private, we include a triage runbook for urgent patches.

9) Sales assets & templates included (links to shared drive)
- 20-minute field deck (template) — use slide flow in section 5.
- 6-week pilot SOW (scoped template).
- Security FAQ one-pager (RFP-ready).
- Cost model spreadsheet (editable) — includes inputs: tokens/day, generation vs embeddings, average token length, expected caching delta.

10) Success metrics for pilot (proposed)
- Latency: p50 < 300ms for generation endpoints in the chosen region.
- Cost: measured $/1M tokens within ±15% of predicted model after caching recommendations.
- Reliability: <1% error rate during pilot and successful rollout of canary policy.
- Validation: product team-completed 10 production-like prompts with pass/fail quality metrics.

11) Ownership & next steps
- Field readiness: SE leader (Marcus Li) owns customizing the deck; commercial lead (Priya Nair) owns pilot SOW and pricing exceptions.
- Playbook actions: schedule technical deep-dive, propose 6-week pilot, assemble security package (KMS config, architecture diagram, evidence).

Appendix: Sample architecture diagrams (text descriptions)
- Hosted-first (fast test): App -> Redwood Hosted API (multi-region) -> model catalog. Suitable for prototypes and first 90-day user tests.
- Dedicated baseline: App -> VPC peering -> Dedicated GPU pool (reserved) -> autoscale worker groups -> metrics -> Redwood Console. Use when predictable throughput is needed.
- Private plane: App (on-prem) -> Private control plane -> on-prem GPU cluster (air-gapped) -> local KMS/HSM integration. Use when data residency and strict network controls are required.

End of document.
